knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For an iid sample from N(μ,σ²), which exact sampling laws are correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the Normal mean and sample-variance laws.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Normal sampling gives exact laws for the mean and scaled variance, plus their independence.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Missing the n-1 scale or forgetting the special Normal-sample independence result.

choices.label: X̄~N(μ,σ²/n), (n-1)S²/σ²~χ²_{n-1}, and X̄ is independent of S².
X̄~N(μ,σ²) because taking a mean does not change variance.
S²/σ²~χ²_n because no scaling by n-1 is required.
X̄ and S² are necessarily dependent for Normal samples because both use the same observations.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.6.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. An iid sample of size n comes from N(μ,σ²). Which statement correctly identifies the exact laws without prematurely using t?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The Normal and chi-square components, with independence, are the ingredients from which the t result is derived.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: State the Normal mean and chi-square variance laws; t comes from their combination.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Calling the unstandardised mean t distributed or treating component laws as the finished t statistic.

choices.label: X̄~N(μ,σ²/n) and (n-1)S²/σ²~χ²_{n-1}, independently. A t law follows only after combining these when σ is unknown.
X̄~t_{n-1} before standardisation because every Normal sample mean has a t distribution.
(n-1)S²/σ²~N(0,1) because sample variance is an average.
The two exact laws finish all t-statistic work even when S has not replaced σ in a standardised mean.
